item.title: Sunday Aftermath: Chiefs' receiver woes, Lamar Jackson's status, and more
item.description: Breaking down all of the NFL's biggest Week 4 storylines, including Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton's injuries.
item.content:encoded:
“Easy” simply does not exist in the NFL. The Bills have the most imposing dual-threat in the history of the game but are slumping on offense. The Eagles’ operation is the envy of the football world and yet the train is off the tracks. The Rams built a summer super team but have had to scratch and claw their way to 2-2.

But perhaps no team’s champagne problems have proved more intractable than the Chiefs and their wideout woes. Since trading Tyreek Hill they’ve won two Super Bowls but had zero 1,000-yard wideouts. They’ve had only one 1,000-yard season of any kind, Travis Kelce’s 1,338-yard 2022. Hell, they haven’t even had a 1,000-yard rushing season in that timespan.

Kenneth Walker III is poised to change that on the ground. Through the air? The slump seems all but guaranteed to continue after a stirring victory over the revitalized Raiders brought the Chiefs to 4-0 but left them without Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton.

Thornton’s injury is the one most emblematic of the Chiefs’ post-Hill problems. A slow-burn reclamation project who was having the best game of his NFL life in Vegas, Thornton was injured on the longest reception of the afternoon and second longest of his career. He didn’t even realize he was hurt until he stood up and saw his own foot pointing in the wrong direction. How do these things keep happening?

So Thornton’s loss has robbed the Chiefs of long-sought depth. Rice’s departure with a hamstring issue is less concerning in the long run but could leave the Chiefs with the league’s very worst receiver corps in the near term. Walker has opened up space and created passing lanes for Patrick Mahomes, but who is he even supposed to throw to? A veteran will undoubtedly be signed, perhaps Hill himself, but there’s a reason you’re available in October.

There are young Dynasty fliers to tantalize fantasy managers in Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen, but again, there’s a reason most casual players have no idea who these people are. It all adds up to a complicated QB1 case for Mahomes, and for a wide receiver fantasy black hole where there should be 2-3 weekly starters.

Five Week 4 Storylines

Lamar Jackson rejoins the injury report. Speaking of never easy. Jackson is well familiar with Mahomes’ receiver woes because he has lived them himself. That includes this season. After the Ravens’ death star opener, they dealt with a limited Zay Flowers for two weeks. Well Flowers was ready to rock on Sunday and the result was 8/118/1 — with Jackson playing only one half. He sat out the second with a supposedly minor ankle injury. That then required a walking boot. That now requires an MRI. This could be standard precaution with a superstar franchise player, but fantasy managers long ago learned nothing is quite standard when it comes to Jackson’s injuries and illnesses. For now, he should be considered on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Falcons, putting Tyler Huntley in the desperation superflex mix.  

Bryce Young’s previously incremental progress begins to appear exponential. Staying on the subject of symbols and struggles, Young is a perfect emblem for how quarterback progress is rarely linear in the 2020s. A complete bust as a 2023 rookie, Young spent the next two years taking one step forward and .75 steps back. He was getting better, but it wasn’t always perceptible to the naked eye. But you don’t need any vision aids to spot this. Young’s great leap forward has finally arrived even if it’s not worth throwing a victory parade over shredding the Lions’ league-worst defense. It is worth pointing out that not only is Young no longer the soft matchup for a struggling defense instead of vice versa, he’s also stacking big time box scores against better teams. Finally looking like the playmaker and problem solver he was at Alabama, Young appears ready for his QB1 closeup.  

Drake Maye tries to get the Patriots’ offense on track. What was happening with Maye was nonsensical enough that you just kind of had to hope he would “snap out of it.” Snap he did vs. the Bills, having his best passing day of the season, his best rushing day of the season, and increasing his 2026 touchdowns total by 300 percent. It was “one game,” but one game that was needed in the worst way. This being the NFL, the good dead was punished with the loss of Mack Hollins to a calf injury, but Maye compensated by playing “2025 ball” and simply spreading the rock around to whomever was open. “Whomever was open” could include A.J. Brown by as early as Week 6. In the meantime, Maye will be back in the low-end QB1 mix against the Raiders.  

Ladd McConkey gets hurt again as Chargers further circle the drain. If Maye was some of the good news on Sunday, his struggle bus counterpart Justin Herbert remained part of the bad. That included an already-limited McConkey aggravating his foot issue. We would say it’s the injury the Chargers could least afford, but then again, it’s an injury they already had. That McConkey kept playing through it was probably foolhardy. Now he seems destined to get some time to rest on the shelf. It’s a brutal blow for fantasy managers and removes any shot Herbert had of returning to QB1 status in the near term. The potential waiver additions — Tre’ Harris, Quentin Johnston, Oronde Gadsden — are all capable of pop-up performances but are unlikely to sustain production for struggling fantasy squads.

Emanuel Wilson carries the mail as Seahawks wait for Zach Charbonnet’s return. The Seahawks’ starting running back, Wilson reached 60 percent of the snaps for the first time this year as he handled a season-high 24 touches. He was not super explosive in the process, but he was not a net negative, either. He mostly kept the chains moving. That, as we’ve learned, is all Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald really cares about in the running game. Charbonnet’s imminent return will immediately hollow out Wilson’s plug-and-play fantasy value, but in the meantime, he looks set to operate as a freebie RB2.  

Don't forget, for the latest on everything NFL, check out Rotoworld’s Player News, or follow @Rotoworld_FB or @RotoPat on Twitter/Bluesky.

Five More Week 4 Storylines

Saquon Barkley gets hurt again as Eagles’ offense plunges to heretofore unseen levels of dysfunction. There are plenty of fancy stats that will tell you how bad the Eagles were against the Rams on Sunday, but a more prosaic one will do — 0-12 on third down. That’s an offense that has no go-to plays or players. It’s a conundrum that would have been unthinkable for the Eagles even last season, and one getting worse instead of better. That’s because Barkley (hamstring) has now joined DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on the shelf. With uncertainty swirling around RT Lane Johnson, things could somehow spiral even further. Making matters even more complicated for fantasy managers is the fact that fill-in RB Tank Bigsby got banged up at the end of yesterday’s contest. Although he and Will Shipley are both worth waivers looks, it is Bigsby who projects to carry the mail on early downs if he can go.  

Bucs’ backfield becomes a confusing mess with Baker Mayfield sidelined. When you’re missing your quarterback, it stands to reason you will rely more on the running game. What the Bucs took that to mean was, what if we make our backfield both more confusing and less productive? That’s what manifested as Bucky Irving played under 60 percent of the snaps for the second consecutive week as Kenneth Gainwell continued to get more involved on passing downs and Sean Tucker re-emerged as a goal-line vulture. Irving was largely trapped between the 20s, which would be a disastrous development for his RB2 value. With Jalon Daniels tabbed for another short-week start against the Cowboys, the only thing keeping Irving hanging around the top 24 is a date with Dallas’ awful run defense.  

DJ Moore gets hurt again, Keon Coleman pops up again. Moore has now failed to finish 50 percent of his first four Bills appearances. He’s been healthy precisely once. The only good news is that Sunday’s injury was an aggravation rather than a new issue. Moore is likely to keep playing through it. He will probably also keep blue tenting through it. Which leaves suddenly resurgent third-year pro Keon Coleman as an intriguing waivers add. This pains me to write as someone who cut Coleman in my Dynasty league after Week 1, but Coleman is doing everything we want out of mid-season receiver additions. He is seeing volume, making big plays, and mixing in some touchdowns. Coleman seems destined to remain inconsistent, but it’s looking like it will be as a WR4 rather than WR40.

Carnell Tate has first good game by any Titan all season. It had gotten to the point that it was difficult to get a single Titan into 12-team league lineups. Tate’s nine-catch, 145-yard performance has at last proven his upside is worth chasing even if Cam Ward is the quarterback. That’s due in part to the fact that though Sunday was the exclamation point, it was a performance Tate had been building towards. Late Round Fantasy’s JJ Zachariason has the defining statistic on that point: “Tate has a 29.6 percent target share this year. The only other rookie wide receivers since 2016 with a higher target share after four games are Malik Nabers, Drake London, and Puka Nacua.” Thank you JJ, and that will do, Carnell, that will do. It’s going to be a wild ride, but maybe Tate can flip you a matchup or two as you deal with byes and injuries elsewhere.  

Ollie Gordon wins the first round with Jaylen Wright. Although Gordon played “just” 56.4 percent of the Dolphins’ snaps, he made them count. He decisively won the touches and routes battle with Wright, and rather improbably contributed the Dolphins’ three longest runs of the season. That included a 53-yard non-scoring rush and 12-yard touchdown. This team is bad enough that no status quo might hold for long — struggling clubs tend to get both desperate and experimental — but Gordon continues to take advantage of the opportunities he has been afforded by De’Von Achane’s loss and Wright’s Week 3 absence.

Early Waivers Look (Players rostered in less than 50 percent of Yahoo leagues)

QB: Kirk Cousins (@NE), Jacoby Brissett (vs. DET), Aaron Rodgers (vs. IND), Geno Smith (vs. CLE), Michael Penix Jr. (vs. BAL), Deshaun Watson (@NYJ)
RB: Emanuel Wilson, Keaton Mitchell, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, Chris Rodriguez Jr., Tyler Allgeier, Brian Robinson Jr., Kimani Vidal, Kaleb Johnson
WR: Adonai Mitchell, Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Malik Washington, Tre Harris, Roman Wilson, Chris Bell, Malachi Fields, Cyrus Allen, Dohnte Meyers
TE: T.J. Hockenson, Michael Mayer, Hunter Henry, Darren Waller, Brenton Strange, Tyler Higbee, Oronde Gadsden
DEF: Bengals (@MIA), Cowboys (vs. TB), Giants (@WAS), Patriots (vs. LV), Browns (@NYJ)

Stats of the Week

Jacoby Brissett is averaging 4.7 yards per attempt on 115 passes since the Cardinals beat the Chargers in Week 1.

Kyren Williams is up to 47 touches over the past two weeks after that number was 28 for Weeks 1 and 2.

We hoped Davante Adams would remain more involved following Puka Nacua’s return, but here are his splits in two games with Nacua in the lineup — 7/58/0 — and two games without: 15/332/2.

Three. That’s how many games in four David Montgomery has played fewer than 60 percent of the Texans’ snaps. He has a 40.4 rushing success rate, putting him just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd and just behind Tony Pollard.

The Jets possessed the ball for just 17:15 against a team starting Tyson Bagent on Sunday. It is the 43rd lowest time of possession in Pro Football Reference's database.

Awards Section

Week 4 Fantasy All-Pro Team: QB Drake Maye, RB Kyren Williams, RB Javonte Williams, WR Tetairoa McMillan, WR CeeDee Lamb, WR Nico Collins, TE T.J. Hockenson

Week 4 All Bank Examiner Squad: QB Justin Herbert, RB Bucky Irving, RB David Montgomery, WR George Pickens, WR Parker Washington, WR Emeka Egbuka, TE Dalton Kincaid

The Spite Decision of the Week: Ben Johnson “starting” Case Keenum solely because he was mad people said he wouldn’t be starting Case Keenum.

Saddest Development of the Week: The Jets finally intercepting a pass and ruining the NFL’s all-time funniest streak.

item.title: Tyson Bagent is expected to start Week 5 vs. Packers
item.description: Ben Johnson isn't going to play the, "Who's going to start?"
item.content:encoded:
Ben Johnson isn't going to play the, "Who's going to start?" game this week.

In a radio interview with ESPN 1000 Chicago on Monday, Johnson said Tyson Bagent will start at quarterback in the team's Week 5 matchup with the Packers.

"Tyson will be the guy," Johnson said, via Kevin Fishbain of TheAthletic.com. "We'll go from there. We're in good shape."

Bagent technically was not the starter on Sunday, as Case Keenum took the first snap in a cheeky move from Johnson. But it was Bagent’s show the rest of the way, as he completed 25-of-34 passes for 268 yards with an interception.

Caleb Williams is dealing with a hamstring injury suffered during the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. He has been considered week-to-week.

In 14 career games with five starts, Bagent has completed 67.2 percent of his passes for 1,239 yards with three touchdowns and seven interceptions.

item.title: Breaking down Bills problems after Week 4; concern or overreaction?
item.description: Should the Bills be concerned with these developments or is concern now an overreaction?
item.content:encoded:
The Bills have the most regular-season wins in the NFL since the start of 2020, and that means a few things.

It establishes how profoundly consistent the team has been during the Josh Allen era. It also quite obviously means there haven’t been many losses over the past six seasons. There is a negative byproduct of that winning, though, particularly when to date it hasn’t amounted to a Super Bowl victory.

When a relatively rare loss does occur, the sky-is-falling phenomenon tends to arise more often than not.

Because Buffalo’s Week 4 loss happened immediately following a shaky performance in a win over the Chargers in Week 3, a lot of concerns have materialized among the fan base and the media. Or are they overreactions?

Here’s how I’d categorize these takes:

Overreaction: Josh Allen isn’t running enough

This was the first takeaway I had from the loss to the Patriots. Is it a situation worth monitoring? Yes. Am I super concerned about it? Not really. In fact, I won’t be surprised if we see an especially run-happy Allen against the Rams and Raiders the next two weeks.

Concern: DJ Moore’s shoulder

An AC joint sprain then an aggravation of that injury in the span of four games for the 29 year old who has been incredibly tough and durable throughout his NFL career. I am starting to wonder if this will be a lingering problem given that this is Year 9 as a professional.

Overreaction: James Cook isn’t getting enough carries

This is one of the most obvious overreactions. The Bills could’ve given the ball to Cook on the ground more than 12 times against the Patriots. Absolutely. I wrote as such in my takeaways article that published this morning.

But he’s seventh in carries through four weeks — pending MNF — and went over 20 carries in back-to-back contests in Weeks 2 and 3. Cook will get his in this Joe Brady offense. Don’t you worry about that.

Overreaction: Dion Dawkins struggling

The past two weeks have represented an unproductive stretch for Dawkins, as he’s allowed nine total pressures. He did lock it down against Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter in Week 1 and held his own against Aidan Hutchinson and Co. against the Lions.

Is Dawkins in the peak prime of his career? No. Can he still play quality football at left tackle for the Bills? Definitely. He’s only 32. Healthy, high-caliber tackles can be valuable assets well into their mid-30s. We’ve seen this little lulls from Dawkins throughout his career. But he doesn’t look slower, or less powerful. He’ll be fine.

Concern: Alec Anderson’s overall play

I have not seen “it” from Anderson through four games. I thought his best performance came against the Lions, but it was mostly when blocking for the run game. That certainly carries its importance. Pass protection is king in the NFL, and the fifth-year pro has been a liability in that area in every contest.

He has found work well — helping out a teammate when he’s left without a defender to block — and laid some devastating blocks in those scenarios. In true one-on-one situations, Anderson has mostly struggled.

The former UCLA Bruin has allowed eight pressures on 152 pass-blocking snaps through four contests. David Edwards allowed four in the first month of the season a year ago.

With Austin Corbett, a nine-year vet with a stable game, waiting in the wings, I wonder how much longer of a leash Anderson has as a full-time starter.

Overreaction: Dalton Kincaid’s sudden drop in production

Three catches for 45 yards including a one-snag, seven-yard performance against the Patriots. A shocking downturn in production from what we saw from Kincaid in the first two weeks of the season.

I don’t think the lacking productivity continues. The sample is large enough to realize that when Kincaid is healthy and on the field, he’s one of the most productive receiving tight ends in football.

Now, does Joe Brady need to dig a little deeper in the playbook or get more creative with how he deploys Kincaid? Absolutely. And I believe he will. No reality check hits harder this time of year for a coach than a loss in the division at home. He’ll start implementing Kincaid as a 1A or 1B option sooner than later, and Kincaid will make plays.

Concern: Max Hairston’s demeanor and post-game reaction

Hairston allowed two touchdowns and four total catches on seven targets in his coverage area. The nonchalance he showed on the game-sealing first down was downright stunning. I am not nor will ever be an analyst who takes it personally when a player doesn’t feel like talking to the media after the game. I do think it can give us an indicator of where a player’s head is at. Apparently Hairston “stormed out” of the locker room after what was clearly a bad performance. He’s allowed to be upset. Of course.

The still very young cornerback needs to understand his job is very much a snap-to-snap gig. He needs to have amnesia out there. Prime example of this came in this contest when Hairston stayed stride for stride with a Patriots receiver on a deep ball and registered a pass breakup before allowing a first down on a dig the very next play. He needs to forget whatever happened on the last play, good or bad, and move forward to his next opportunity in coverage. Or to make a tackle in space.

And it’s almost if he’s playing too tentatively even if off-coverage. Hairston has freaky physical talent. Twitchy as it gets at the cornerback spot. But for as much as he could rely on that explosion in the SEC to make plays on the football when planting and driving on a comeback route toward the sideline, or in-breaker… he can’t regularly do that in the NFL. He has to be more situationally aware and mentally strong to accentuate all his robust skills. Those two elements are more concerning to me than his actual play, believe it or not.

If he can get right mentally, I truly believe Hairston will be fine.

Overreaction: Josh Allen’s decision-making

Contrary to popular belief in and around Western New York, among Bills Mafia, and, really, the entire football-watching population, Allen is not a flawless football player.

He’s not going to make the perfect decision 100% of the time.

And Allen did not become the superstar he is today because of his decision-making specialty anyway. Much more often than not, the Bills quarterback makes the right decision. The enormous sample size of his career tells us that. I’m not concerned about his clearly bad decision on the interception on Buffalo’s final drive of the Week 4 loss.

Concern: Terrel Bernard’s lack of explosiveness

Bernard is first on the team in tackles and third in stops (tackles that constitute a “loss” for the defense based on down and distance). But I can’t shake some of the reps I saw live — and on the in-stadium replay — from Bernard the past two weeks.

What were those reps exactly? Outside runs or quick throws to tight ends or receivers in which Bernard had a free run to the ball-carrier and simply couldn’t get to the football in time before the offensive player could turn upfield for a solid gain.

Sure, it could be Bernard still learning the intricacies of Jim Leonhard’s defense which is slowing the speed at which he reads and reacts to his keys. But he doesn’t appear as explosive or fast as he was even a few years ago. In coverage too.

Overreaction: WR screens are back!

Entering this Week 4 game, the Bills offense was below the league average in screen rate. Sure, the few thrown against the Patriots could conceivably move Buffalo closer to league average. But Allen isn’t utilizing screens at an alarmingly predictable frequency. And a screen — to a RB or WR — is a very viable play every team should have in its playbook and probably utilize every week.

Plus, Connor McGovern confirmed on WGR 550 this was not the called play in the huddle. It was an audible based on the look the Patriots defense gave the Bills. Do the Bills want to have something other than a quick screen to a WR dialed up if they see a max pressure look from the defense on third down? Yes.

item.title: Fantasy Football: Emanuel Wilson takes over Seahawks' backfield, plus more key stats to note from Week 4
item.description: Joel Smyth takes you through 10 stats to note from Week 4 to help with fantasy football.
item.content:encoded:
In fantasy football, you have to look back to move forward. Fantasy points are the goal, but how a player gets there is the key. Analyst Joel Smyth breaks down 10 numbers to know from Week 4 in order to win your matchup in Week 5 and beyond.

100%

Of the Jets' RB touches went to Braelon Allen, only the second RB this season to have a game with 100% of the backfield touches (Week 2 James Cook). It may not have been a pretty game for the Jets offense, but Allen should gain some trust for fantasy managers. New York had less than 17 minutes of possession time and a league-wide, season-low 32 offensive snaps played. Of those 32 snaps, Allen saw 14 carries and two receptions, tallying 68 scrimmage yards.

I fully expected RB Isaiah Davis to come in for a third of the work and a good amount of the receiving downs, but Frank Reich and Co. decided they wanted Allen in there for every single play to replace Breece Hall. With a game against Cleveland next week, I'd be happy to flex Allen.

The Jets had 32 plays in Week 4, the 4th fewest in a game in the @Stathead database in NFL history.

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) October 5, 2026

75%

Of Seattle's RB touches went to Emanuel Wilson, the first Seahawk bell cow since playoff Kenneth Walker. George Holani was no more than a third-down back with Jadarian Price out. As long as Zach Charbonnet and Price are sidelined, Wilson can be comfortably used in this dynamic offense. The most surprising usage came in the passing game, as Wilson went from one target in Weeks 1-3 to four in his first start of the season. He paid it off too, with three receptions, 39 yards and a TD.

The 75% share was good for 25 total touches as Seattle controlled the game, something it should manage to do going forward.

68-55

The Arizona RB route split this season, favoring Tyler Allgeier. Jeremiyah Love is fun to watch and the Cardinals' coaching staff is still keeping us asking for more. After a workhorse day in Week 3, Arizona went back to using a healthy amount of Allgeier, staying true to their "hot hand" mentality. The most surprising part of the usage, however, has been the receiving game. Love was one of the best receiving backs in the country last season at Notre Dame, yet Allgeier is being used as a passing-down back despite entering the season averaging 17 targets a year. With only 36 receiving yards on the season, the rookie becomes far more volatile than we'd want.

At the same time, if you trade for him and he does start getting a bump in his receiving usage, he could be a game-changer even with carries and red-zone work being split.

4.2

Average depth of target in Jalon Daniels' first career start. It may be a tough stretch here for Emeka Egbuka. On 36 dropbacks, Daniels had 148 pass yards, most coming off of the quick-passing attack. With Egbuka being more reliant on the downfield targets, he ended his day with only two catches for 13 yards on four targets. He wasn't playing that great with Baker Mayfield to begin with, but I would not put Egbuka in my starting lineup for the time being with Mayfield sidelined.

27-13

The carry split in Philadelphia after two games with Saquon Barkley exiting early. Tank Bigsby at 27 (14 and 13) and Will Shipley at 13 (6 and 7). It's been nearly identical in both games and gives us a clear picture of their potential going forward. Bigsby is the RB you want on waivers. He's not going to get the receiving role, but if we're real, Hurts isn't going to throw much to the RB anyway. Bigsby should have the goal-line role (so far, 1-of-1 attempt) and can be a solid flex play in most leagues. Shipley will likely keep him from being a fantasy star, but both are worth a pickup if Barkley is out.

79%

Josh Downs route share this season. He'll be okay. Annoying, yes, but I'm not panicking about Downs' Week 4 dud too much going forward. The Commanders' secondary that has been torched this season didn't allow Daniel Jones to push the ball downfield to Downs at all, amassing one singular air yard after 154 in Week 3. That'll be the key for Downs, who will always have the short targets available, but starts to rake in fantasy points when targeted downfield on top of it. The international games also tend to provide a few questionable performances, if it helps to cope a little bit easier.​

3

Red-zone targets for Romeo Doubs. The Patriots' new WR rose to the occasion, capitalizing on Drake Maye's bounce-back performance versus a Bills defense. It's been a slow start to the season, but there's plenty of hope with both A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins sidelined. Did you know there are only seven more WRs with more red-zone touchdowns since 2023 than Doubs?

He's always been a threat in the red area, pulling in another one TD on Sunday on a goal-line fade. If New England builds this offense back up, Doubs can be the main benefactor in the red zone.

A reminder: Maye had only one passing touchdown in the first three games. Doubs now has two of Maye's four on the season, as he now becomes the clear WR1 of this offense until Brown returns.

12.5%

Targets per route for Dalton Kincaid over the last two weeks. Unlike in the past, his route share hasn't been the issue. Joe Brady spoke to the postgame press after Week 4, openly saying they need to get Kincaid more targets. His targets per route in 2025 finished at 24.3%, just 0.4% from the highest TE mark, while playing through injuries. After starting the year at 29.2%, I'm not overly worried about the last two weeks. Unlike other TEs, Kincaid runs most of his routes lined up as a pure WR, and isn't immune to down games in a low-passing-volume offense.

Josh Allen also just has one passing touchdown in the last two games, affecting the passing game as a whole.

77%

Kyren Williams' percentage of the Rams' RB touches over the last two weeks. One last RB touch stat. Over the first two weeks, that share was 49%, very similar to the second half of the 2025 season. It's not just that Williams takes all of the receiving, but he has 31 of the 41 carries these last two weeks, making Blake Corum an afterthought, and Williams a force on one of the league's top offenses. Only eight RBs have that high of volume to begin this season.

Another factor that's boosted his stock is the passing-game usage. The Rams, year after year, have been near the bottom in RB target share, but after another strong receiving performance, Williams' targets per game have doubled since last season, although most of that has been the last two weeks. Last year, he only had one game over three receptions, and he's done that and more in back-to-back weeks.

54

Routes for Dohnte Meyers, the most of any player in Week 4. If you're asking, "Who?" Meyers is the Bengals' rookie WR who came out of nowhere and shined among all the Bengals' WR injuries. Meyers began the season as the WR4, and may begin Week 5 as the WR1.

He's a shifty, YAC receiver who brought in seven of nine targets for 82 yards this week. The Bengals are going to throw no matter who's out there and Meyers has proved he can make plays with the ball in his hands. If Tee Higgins or Ja'Marr Chase are out (potentially both could miss Week 5), Meyers can be a fun fill-in play versus the Dolphins.

item.title: Week 5 NFL betting, odds: Bears are favorites against Packers at Lambeau Field for first time in 20 years
item.description: The Chicago Bears are short road favorites at Lambeau Field -- something that hasn't happened since the Bears went to the Super Bowl in 2006.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears moved to 3-1 on the season with a dominant 23-12 win at Soldier Field over the New York Jets on Sunday. The Bears had a remarkable 34 first downs (to the Jets' seven) and 492 yards of total offense to New York's 157.

The Green Bay Packers improved to 2-2 on the season with a far less impressive 17-14 road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and rookie QB Jalon Daniels. Respected money came in on Tampa Bay to push the line down to Packers -2.5, so Green Bay ended up covering the closing line. That was the Packers' first win against the spread this season.

Chicago heads to Green Bay in Week 5 and the Bears were 2.5-point favorites at sportsbooks on Monday morning. Why is this notable?

Because if the line holds, it would be the first time that the Bears have been favored at Lambeau Field in over 20 years.

Yes, the last time that Chicago walked into Green Bay as a favorite was back on Sept. 10, 2006 — Week 1 of that season — when the Bears closed as 3.5-point favorites. Chicago won that game 26-0 thanks to 262 passing yards from Rex Grossman, two Brett Favre interceptions and a Packers lost fumble. That season ended for the Bears in the Super Bowl — a 29-17 loss to Peyton Manning and the Indianapolis Colts.

The Bears are 3-1 against the spread this season, and have won games straight-up and ATS with Caleb Williams, Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent starting.

Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury against the Minnesota Vikings in a Week 2 loss, and was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Jets. Head coach Ben Johnson confirmed on Monday that Bagent will start again on Sunday against Green Bay.

The Packers were a three-point home favorite this offseason in the lookahead lines at DraftKings Sportsbook.

item.title: Steelers sign CB Sean Murphy-Bunting off Bucs practice squad
item.description: After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, help is on the way for Pittsburgh’s secondary.
item.content:encoded:
After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, help is on the way for Pittsburgh’s secondary.

Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the Steelers are signing cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting off of the Buccaneers’ practice squad.

Murphy-Bunting, 29, missed the 2025 season with a torn ACL. He had returned to the Buccaneers after he was released by the Cardinals at roster cuts in August.

A second-round pick in 2019, Murphy-Bunting has appeared in 82 career games with 65 starts. In 2024, he registered 52 total tackles with three interceptions, five passes defensed, and two forced fumbles in 15 games for the Cardinals.

He has 34 career passes defensed with 11 career interceptions.

item.title: Ben Johnson made QB Case Keenum the Bears starter for 1 snap for extremely petty reason
item.description: Only Ben Johnson would do this.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears had a quarterback decision to make heading into their Week 4 game against the New York Jets. With starter Caleb Williams still sidelined by a very real hamstring strain, head coach Ben Johnson had to choose between Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent. Bagent ended training camp No. 2 on the depth chart, but suffered a concussion after he spelled Williams in Week 2. That opened the door for Keenum to start Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which turned into a magical night for the 38-year-old in a brilliant performance to lead the Bears to an unlikely win.

Could Keenum really do it again? Did Bagent really deserve to lose his backup job because of an injury? Johnson played his cards close to the vest all week, but reports circulated at the end of the week that Bagent would be the starter.

Those reports pissed off Johnson. When the Bears came out for the first possession of the game, it was Keenum lined up under center while Bagent was playing wide receiver. Keenum handed the ball off for a short gain, and it was the only snap he took all afternoon. Bagent took over from there, and the Bears demolished the Jets 23-12.

Johnson was asked about why Keenum took the first snap of the game, and described it as a “ceremonial first pitch.” He mostly made the decision to mess with the media reports leading into the week. Watch Johnson’s press conference clip here:

“I got all these memos saying Tyson was starting before I ever made an announcement,” Johnson said. “So I wanted to get Case out there first time.”

The reporters in the press conference quickly noted that Johnson’s plan meant Keenum — not Bagent — earned the win. Johnson is a data nerd who probably hates the idea of wins as a QB stat more than anyone. He immediately said it was a team win, and a convincing one for Chicago at that.

Johnson’s ploy to start the game did put an asterisk on the Bears’ win in the history books. According to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune, the Bears would have become the third team since 1950 to have three quarterbacks win in the first four games of the season … but not Keenum gets credit for the win over the Jets, not Bagent. Johnson won’t care about that at all. He’s just happy his team could keep it humming with another new QB against a Jets team that has been a little feistier than expected.

Johnson is a psychopath in the best way possible. He spoke openly about wanting to set the NFL scoring record coming into this season, and while Williams’ injury might derail that, he’s still doing incredible things with this team. Some of these stats via Biggs and the Tribune are just unbelievable. The win over the Jets was not nearly as close as the final score indicated. The Bears had more first downs (34) than the Jets did total plays (32). Chicago won the time of possession battle 42:45 to 17:15. The Bears didn’t punt. The Jets’ 32 plays is the fourth-lowest total in NFL history. The Bears ran 57 more plays than the Jets, the second biggest margin in league history.

The Bears’ win in Week 3 with Keenum under center proved Johnson is an elite NFL head coach early into his second season. Their win over the Jets with Bagent at QB feels like it certifies Chicago as a true Super Bowl contender. The Bears are far from perfect, but the defense has been better than expected and it’s clear Johnson can draw up a good game plan regardless of who is playing QB. If Williams can come back healthy and regain his form as a potential top-10 quarterback league-wide, the Bears will be right there with the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks in the NFC.

Landing Johnson and Williams together feels too good to be true for Bears fans who suffered through the Marc Trestman, John Fox, and Matt Eberflus eras recently. This team is cooking, and we haven’t even seen them at their best yet. That’s a scary thought, and it’s largely because of Johnson’s remarkable competence at head coach.

item.title: Report: Kyle Juszczyk could miss a couple of weeks with knee injury
item.description: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk had to leave Sunday's win over the Broncos with a knee injury, but early indications are that he will avoid a long absence from the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk had to leave Sunday's win over the Broncos with a knee injury, but early indications are that he will avoid a long absence from the lineup.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Juszczyk's ACL and other ligaments appeared to be intact. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that initial tests showed that Juszczyk hyperextended his knee and that he is expected to miss a couple of weeks, but still needs to have an MRI to confirm that belief.

Any missed time for Juszczyk would force Shanahan and the 49ers to alter some offensive plans, but they've become adept at that this year and in past years due to an extended run of injuries across the roster.

Juszczyk had two catches for 28 yards Sunday and he has four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown this season.

item.title: The Rams need to beat the Bills
item.description: The Rams can’t take the road to the wild card if they want to be the Super Bowl champions they were predicted to be
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is only entering Week 5, but the October stakes couldn’t be higher for the NFC West based on next weekend’s games. The Los Angeles Rams salvaged potential disaster by coming back to beat the Philadelphia Eagles and setting their record at 2-2, and they’re within striking distance of the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-1 Seattle Seahawks.

However, that slim margin could become a chasm if the Rams lose to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5.

Worst Case: 49ers 5-0, Rams 2-3

The 49ers already have a head-to-head advantage by beating the Rams 27-7 in Week 1. So already the Rams are in a position where they are in a must-win situation when they face San Francisco in Week 14 — but a lot could change by then.

Either in L.A.’s favor or against it. Starting this weekend.

Week 5: 49ers at Seahawks

Week 5: Bills at Rams

If the 49ers beat the Seahawks, and the Bills beat the Rams, then L.A. will essentially already be four games back of first place in the NFC West. Four, not three.

That’s 3 games back in the win-loss column + a head-to-head loss.

Things get really, really ugly when a team is that far behind another team at any point in the season.

The good news about it being early in the season is that there’s a lot of time for things to change.

The bad news is that it could get that bad this early in the season?

The Rams are not in must-win territory, especially when it comes to simply making the playoffs (and it should NOT be the goal for L.A. to only make the playoffs, they must do much better than that), but Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are pushing the envelope if they lose to the Bills.

And the Bills are not going to be easy to beat.

Odds to NFC West if this happens: 8.5%

If the 49ers end up 5-0 and the Rams 2-3, then L.A.’s odds to win the NFC West drop to approximately 8.5%. This isn’t easy to calculate because a lot depends on whether or not the Rams win the rematch. Even if the Rams win that game, the odds only go up to about 12%. If the Rams lose the rematch, then their odds to win the NFC West are almost 0.

But think of it like this based on the 5-0 vs. 2-3 scenario:

If the 49ers go 10-2 the rest of the way, the Rams can’t win the division

If the 49ers go 9-3 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 12-0

If the 49ers go 8-4 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 11-1

If the 49ers go 7-5 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 10-2

It becomes a situation where the Rams have to be almost perfect and they need the 49ers to play significantly worse than they’ve already played this season.

And that’s just looking at ONE team. The Rams also have to be better than the Seahawks to win the division.

“So what? Just win a wild card!”

Here we go again: The “All-In” Rams going for…a wild card?

Wild Card teams don’t win

The Rams haven’t won or reached the Super Bowl since 2021, when they won the division and were the number four seed. That team also had two home games in the playoffs, including the NFC Championship against the 49ers. L.A. can’t count on getting a home game if they are a wild card, and it’s exceedingly rare for teams to go 3-0 on the road in the playoffs.

Like it just doesn’t happen.

Since 2021’s 7-team playoff expansion, a wild card has NOT made the Super Bowl.

From 2002-2020, wild card teams reached the Super Bowl only 4 times (05 PIT, 07 NYG, 10 GB, 20 TB).

So since 2002 realignment, only four wild card teams have reached the Super Bowl. And since expanding the schedule to include an extra wild card, a wild card teams has not even reached the Super Bowl.

The goal NEEDS to be winning the NFC West.

If the Rams lose to the Bills, that becomes extremely difficult to do. Especially if the 49ers beat the Seahawks.

Bills 3-1

Buffalo dropped to 3-1 after losing to the Patriots 29-26 on Sunday. It was a close game, obviously, and needed an exceptional catch by New England’s rookie receiver to win the game in the final minute.

On offense, the Bills have Josh Allen and James Cook and they lead the NFL in points per game.

On defense, the Bills are 25th in points allowed per game. Buffalo has allowed at least 29 points in three of four games, with the only exception being the hapless L.A. Chargers.

The Bills are hard to beat. The Rams need to beat them. If McVay and Stafford L.A. to a win, then the Rams will be a threat to win the NFC West regardless of how Seattle vs. San Francisco goes because then we’ll know that the team is waking up. However, if they sleep through this week and lose, the odds of getting the rebound that they need to have will be dramatically deflated.

item.title: Commanders vs. Colts (London) – Studs and Duds
item.description: Washington took on Indianapolis over the pond and, although they hung tough early on, the injuries (playing their third string quarterback), inconsistent play calling, poor coaching and having to play not only against the Colts but also the refs, ultimately doomed the Commanders in the end and resulted in a 30-13 loss. Washington is now […]
item.content:encoded:
Washington took on Indianapolis over the pond and, although they hung tough early on, the injuries (playing their third string quarterback), inconsistent play calling, poor coaching and having to play not only against the Colts but also the refs, ultimately doomed the Commanders in the end and resulted in a 30-13 loss.

Washington is now 1-3 on the season with a division game against the Giants on the horizon. Dan Quinn’s seat continues to get even hotter and Adam Peters’ draft and free-agency strategy have fans questioning his qualifications.

Although there is a great chance both quarterback Jayden Daniels and receiver Terry McLaurin return next week, it’s going to take a miracle for Washington to make the postseason at this rate.

Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes.

Studs:

  • CB Amik Robertson: Mik led the team in tackles (nine total, seven solo) and had a beautiful pass defended on a deep shot down the left sideline, allowing just two passes completed in coverage. He continues to be the bright spot on this defense.
  • DL Javon Kinlaw: Kinlaw has been playing some really good football, and that continued over the pond. He recorded three tackles (two of them stops), had two batted passes and two pressures.
  • CB Rasul Douglas: Douglas had a nice game against Indy’s wide receivers. He recorded an interception on an errant pass by Jones and had a big hit to prevent a first down on a third-and-short. He had six tackles and a pass defensed.

Duds:

  • Alan Eck and his crew: This was easily the worst officiated game I have seen in quite some time, and I have seen some bad ones throughout the years. This crew, led by the Pennsylvania guy who grew up an Eagles fan, called a completely one-sided game that saw Washington get hit with 10 penalties for 84 yards and had a touchdown by Antonio Williams erased, while the Colts had just one penalty for five yards. But it wasn’t just what was called. It’s also what wasn’t called, including two pretty blatant pass interference calls against the Colts defensive backs. The “crew” needs to be investigated by the NFL.
  • HC Dan Quinn/OC David Blough: The fourth-down run with none other than CRAIG REYNOLDS behind the weak spot on our offensive line was mind-blowingly STUPID! Also, why are we not using our tight ends in the passing game? I still like Blough and know he’s being hamstrung by who/what he’s being given, but as for Quinn, his time is running out.
  • G Matt Gulbin: It was a rough start for the rookie at right guard (and this speaks to just how bad Nick Allegretti has been playing), and although his play did improve some as the game went on, it wasn’t nearly enough to keep him off the Duds list. His lack of blocking is what got Mariota injured early on.
  • P Tress Way: Way was “WAY” off with his punting throughout the game. This may be the first time he’s made my Duds list, but he definitely deserved it.
  • GM Adam Peters: Peters and Quinn lied to us all offseason about Nick “The Wonder-Boy” Allegretti”, and how they had FULL CONFIDENCE in him as their starting center. Four weeks into the season, a street free agent has taken over at center and Wonder-Boy was benched at right guard for a rookie. Not only that, but Adam went into the season with almost $26M in cap space, yet proceeded to sign guys off the street who are now starting. His draft picks have turned out to be just BAD (Sainritsil, Sinnott and McCaffrey), while others can’t see the field because they are injured (Daniels, Amos, Newton and Magee). Bill Croskey-Merritt is not RB1, yet were treating him as if he is. Coleman is serviceable at best as a left tackle. At some point, the finger needs to be pointed in his direction for his poor personnel decisions – including his trade for an injured Lattimore.

Notes:

  • QB Athan Kaliakmanis had an up-and-down game, but given the circumstances, I though the rookie hung in there and did the best he could. He made some good throws and he made a few I’m sure he’d like to have back. I’ll tell ya what though: he’s not afraid to let it rip!
  • QB Marcus Mariota looked good early in the game before getting his knee injured. I believe we win this game with him under center for all four quarters.
  • DL Daron Payne looked a bit better against the Colts, getting some good push in the pocket. He registered three pressures on the afternoon and had some nice tackles.
  • EDGE Odafe Oweh had a rather quite game, but he did have the hat-trick early in the first quarter where he pushed his defended into Jones — registering a sack, forced fumble and fumble recovery on the play. He notched two pressures on the afternoon.
  • RB Austin Ekeler, in limited action, looked like the best running back on the roster. This is a direct indictment on Adam Peters for not adequately addressing the position in the offseason.
  • WR Dyami Brown had a good game given the situation. He had caught three of his four targets for 65 yards.
  • How is it that LB Sonny Sytles (reigning NFC Defensive Player of the Week) and LB Kain Medrano were splitting time in Nickle, while Luvu was on the field for 100% of the snaps? Please, make this make sense!
  • WR Antonio Williams is going to be a really solid receiver. His long run-after-the-catch touchdown that got brought back for two phantom penalties was really nice.
  • I thought S Jeremy Reaves had a rough start to the season, but he’s shown well over the last two week – and I know he’s playing a bit dinged-up. Props to Revo for toughing it out.
  • EDGEK’Lavon Chaisson remained active against the Colts despite being held (not called – big surprise) most of the game. He combined with Tim Settle for a sack and had three pressures.
  • K Drew Stevens hit both of his field goals with a long of 31. Hey, right now I’m looking for as many positives as I can find…
  • CB Mike Sainristil played just five defensive snaps. He’s on his way to being inactive, maybe even released.

The Saints currently have a record of 1-2, with their game against the Atlanta Falcons set for Monday Night Football this evening in New Orleans. All of their games this season have been close ones. They started this season with a 31-30 overtime loss in Detroit, as their two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game in overtime was unsuccessful. They followed that up with a 24-17 victory in Baltimore over the Ravens before falling at home to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3 by a score of 35-27. In their two losses, they turned the ball over seven times, including three interceptions from quarterback Tyler Shough and three lost fumbles in their loss to the Raiders.

The Vikings, on the other hand, continue winning despite an almost complete lack of offense. In two of their four victories this season, they have failed to score an offensive touchdown. In order to find a team that’s done that and gotten off to a 4-0 start, you have to go back to before the Great Depression, as the feat was accomplished by the 1922 and 1923 Chicago Cardinals. The Vikings have scored just one offensive touchdown in their last three games, but a combination of special teams and Brian Flores’ suffocating defense have kept the purple among the league’s undefeated through the first four weeks of the season.

This will be the last game for the Vikings before their early bye week, as they’ll be off in Week 6. They’ll be back in the early window of broadcast action this week, as this one is scheduled for noon Central Time on the FOX family of networks.

item.title: Broncos WR Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle and will miss a ‘few weeks’
item.description: According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle during the Broncos’ loss to the 49ers on Sunday and is expected to miss “a few weeks”. Bryant was carted off the field after the injury, which did not look all that good on the replay, and […]
item.content:encoded:
According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant suffered a sprained ankle during the Broncos’ loss to the 49ers on Sunday and is expected to miss “a few weeks”.

Bryant was carted off the field after the injury, which did not look all that good on the replay, and he seemed to have suffered a potentially serious knee injury. However, we learned late last night that the belief was that neither he nor cornerback Pat Surtain II suffered season-ending injuries, and for Bryant, that was confirmed today.

Honestly, this is about as best-case as you can get with this injury. It looked bad, and I assumed Bryant’s season was done. Thankfully, it’s just a sprained ankle, and he will miss a few weeks. It remains to be seen if Bryant will land on the short-term injured reserve or not, but we will learn that in the coming days.

The Broncos play the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday and then play the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks on a short week on Thursday Night Football. Bryant will likely be sidelined for both of these games, at least, but after that, we will have to see.

This is still a tough loss for the Broncos’ scuffling offense. Bryant has been one of their more consistent and productive playmakers in recent weeks and just finished making a big play before suffering this sprained ankle. So, they will need Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims, and/or Lil’Jordan Humphrey to step up while he is sidelined.

We are still awaiting word on the severity of CB Pat Surtain II’s ankle injury and CB Riley Moss’s rib injury. Again, the belief is that Surtain II did not suffer an Achilles injury, which is great, but he is still expected to miss some time. We will have that update when we get more information, but in the meantime, we can be thankful that Bryant escaped with just a sprained ankle and should be back on the field after a few weeks.

item.title: Mike Vrabel replies to Bills player who dismissed Patriots WR's incredible catch

item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills played on Sunday, Oct. 4. The matchup continued with a war of words into the next day.

First, Bills cornerback C.J. Gardner-Johnson – a lightning rod no matter which jersey he wears – chalked up his team's 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday, Oct. 4 to a "practice squad player" making "a hell of a play," as Efton Chism III caught the game-winning touchdown from Drake Maye with 1:50 on the clock.

"We're not going to get into any bulletin board material," Gardner-Johnson said – before doing exactly that. "An elevated guy made a hell of a catch – probably won't hear from him again.

"A practice squad player made a hell of a play. That's all I'm going to tell you. You do it again, and he probably won't make it again."

Gardner-Johnson, who won Super Bowl 59 as a member of the Philadelphia Eagles, also claimed that the Patriots didn't "do (expletive) better than us."

During his normal Monday appearance on Boston local radio station WEEI, Patriots head coach Vrabel fired back.

"For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill," the 2025 Coach of the Year said.

#Patriots HC Mike Vrabel responds to #Bills DB C.J. Gardner-Johnson calling WR Efton Chism a practice-squad player:

Vrabel went on to praise Chism's work ethic during practice and claimed that, according to the tracking data from practice, nobody runs more throughout the week.

Injuries to A.J. Brown, who has been out since Week 1, and Mack Hollins, injured during the Bills game, created the opportunity for Chism – who made the most of it. The second-year player from Eastern Washington has seven career catches, two of them going for touchdowns.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw says he told Sean Payton to 'get the f*** off the field' during testy postgame exchange
item.description: Dre Greenlaw did not enjoy his one season in Denver.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers remained undefeated Sunday, picking up a big 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos. It's safe to say no one celebrated that victory more than 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw.

The 29-year-old admitted he took the contest personally after spending an injury-riddled 2025 season with the Broncos and head coach Sean Payton. While Greenlaw said he harbored no ill will toward his former Broncos teammates, Payton was a different story.

Greenlaw made no attempt to hide that during the contest. After a particular play near the Broncos' sideline, Greenlaw appeared to point at and exchange words with Payton.

Dre Greenlaw clearly took this game personally against the Broncos and Sean Payton. pic.twitter.com/pKbCuIVF42

— Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 4, 2026

Things escalated after the game, when it appeared Greenlaw had to be dragged away by Fred Warner after taunting Payton at midfield.

Warning: Video contains some NSFW language.

#49ers LB Dre Greenlaw had to be held back by Fred Warner after today's game as he celebrated in front of Sean Payton.

Greenlaw made it clear that today’s game against the Broncos—the team he played for last season—was personal.

(📽️ @Romi_Bean)pic.twitter.com/caaljYrfDK

— Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 5, 2026

Greenlaw explained his actions after the contest, and revealed what he told Payton in the above clip. Greenlaw said he told Payton to "get the f*** off the field" after the 49ers' win, according to the San Francisco Chronicle.

"I told him to get the f*** off the field," Greenlaw said. "That's it: 'Get the f*** off the field.'"

The linebacker also explained why the game meant so much to him. Greenlaw said it stemmed from how he was treated by Payton during an injury-riddled 2025 season. Greenlaw said it reached a point where Payton wouldn't interact with him while he was out.

When it came time for the Broncos to move forward without Greenlaw, the linebacker said he received the news he was being cut from his agent. Greenlaw called it "disrespectful" that Payton wasn't the one to deliver that message to the linebacker.

After spending his entire career with the 49ers, Greenlaw signed a three-year, $35 million deal with the Broncos for the 2025 NFL season. He missed time early in the year with a quad injury and also missed time late in the season with a hamstring issue. He was released by the team after just one season.

Greenlaw apparently took out all his frustrations on Payton during the game, as the linebacker led the 49ers with 12 tackles — seven solo. He also forced a fumble in the victory.

item.title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week four loss
item.description: Zach Sieler shows out, while Miami’s special teams displays warts once again.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins fell to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday by a score of 15-10. While keeping it close only really counts in horseshoes and hand-grenades, as they say, it was Miami’s narrowest defeat of the season through four tough contests. This team is getting better, despite the considerable limitations they are under regarding the mammoth amount of dead cap they are currently dealing with, and I don’t think it’s long before they steal a victory to finally get into the win column this year.

Of course there are still glaring problems on this team — covering tight ends has been one of those problems. T.J. Hockenson was targeted 13 times yesterday — he caught all 13 passes for a game high 119 yards receiving. Special teams is another — with multiple errors leading to fantastic starting field position for the Vikings on numerous occasions.

FINS UP

Our Fins Up player from Miami’s week three loss is defensive tackle Zach Sieler. It had been a rough start to the season for Miami’s veteran defender, however, on Sunday against the Vikings, Sieler unleashed his frustrations on Minnesota quarterback Kyler Murray — sacking the diminutive passer twice on the afternoon to account for half of Miami’s four sacks on the day.

Sieler hadn’t sacked an opposing quarterback since Week 16 of last season. He finished last season with just 5.5 sacks after having 10 sacks in both the 2023 and 2024 seasons. If he can continue the momentum he began building on Sunday, Miami’s monster in the middle could easily surpass last year’s sack total in short order.

FINS DOWN

This week’s Fins Down personality is once again special teams coordinator Chris Tabor. Tabor, a respected coach in the National Football League, has now been named in our Fins Down section twice this season — also earning the dubious distinction after week one’s dismal performance from his unit.

All afternoon long, Minnesota’s offense was treated to great starting field position due to Miami’s inability to cover kick returns with any competency. Tabor is working with what he has — and what he has is a bunch of young, inexperienced football players trying to make their mark on an undermanned Dolphins squad. However, it is his job to coach them up and maximize their abilities. Unfortunately, he isn’t doing such a great job at that just yet…

His next opportunity to show that he should remain on Miami’s staff will come this Sunday when the Dolphins host the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium.

Offense

Jackson played all 33 snaps in the first half but did not return after halftime with an ankle injury. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley (31 snaps) played the final two quarters. The Ravens suffered another offensive line injury as Andrew Vorhees exited after 28 snaps with a foot ailment and did not return. That forced Emery Jones to plug in at right guard, where he played 36 snaps. Carson Vinson played two snaps as an extra blocker upon Ronnie Stanley’s return to the starting lineup.

After playing limited snaps in Week 3, Zay Flowers’ workload increased as he led all wide receivers in playing time (47 snaps). Devontez Walker saw a big jump in playing time with 44 snaps, 14 more than Rashod Bateman (30 snaps). Bateman got shaken up at one point in the game. Rookie Elijah Sarratt played a season-high 23 snaps and made his first NFL catch for 13 yards. Chris Moore was inactive for this game.

Matthew Hibner’s 37 snaps were a season-high at tight end and he matched Mark Andrews in playing time. The latter caught five passes with a touchdown grab, while Hibner recorded 34 receiving yards. Durham Smythe suffered an achilles injury after 18 snaps and did not return. If Smythe is out long-term, expect Hibner and Josh Cuevas to quickly take on larger roles.

With Trey Hendrickson (finger) inactive, Mike Green saw a significant role expansion (41 snaps). He had a team-high six pressures and three quarterback hits.
