Roquan Smith went the distance as usual with 64 snaps at linebacker, followed by Trenton Simpson (36) and Teddye Buchanan (11). Simpson had a team-high nine tackles and logged an interception, continuing his strong start to the season. Buchanan saw a few more snaps than last week in his second game back from injury.

At cornerback, Marlon Humphrey suffered a calf injury after just eight snaps and did not return. That forced Chidobe Awuzie to start the remainder of the game (56 snaps) alongside Nate Wiggins, who played all 64 snaps. Rookie Chandler Rivers played 29 snaps in the slot. The Ravens continue to opt for four cornerbacks and four safeties in the secondary rotation. Jaylinn Hawkins saw his snap share decrease as the No. 3 safety (45 snaps) and K’Von Wallace received two defensive snaps in the mix.

item.title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ win over the Bills
item.description: Notes, musings, and observations from New England’s win over the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Covering the NFL, in any capacity, is like being a weatherman. You don’t know a damn thing and you’re wrong more often than you’re right. But since nobody else knows anything either, you get a pass each and every week.

The New England Patriots, who have been struggling all season and were without their best cornerback and best interior linemen on both sides of the ball, took the best team in the AFC to the wire yesterday in a game that should give us all a lot of optimism going forward. It’s kind of fitting that Buffalo’s first-ever loss in their new stadium came at the hands of the Patriots, the team that won the most games ever at the old Bills stadium.

  1. I feel like everyone, yours truly included, had the Patriots sitting at 2-2 through four weeks. Lo and behold, here we find ourselves. Did I think New England would get slapped around by Jacksonville only to beat Buffalo on the road? Of course not. But that’s why we watch this nonsensical sport.
  2. If there’s a larger chasm that separates a 2-2 team from a 1-3 team, I don’t know what it is. It’s technically only one game, but teams sitting at 1-3 this morning are taking a long, unshaven, hungover look in the mirror right now, while the 2-2 teams are motivated to position themselves for a strong October.
  3. So, this game meant more than just getting a divisional win on the road, for a lot of reasons. But before I get into why that is, I’ll own my blatant sports fan hypocrisy by admitting that I would have spin-zoned the hell out of this game if Buffalo had won it. Drake Maye looked more poised. They hung with one of the best teams in the AFC. Lots to build on. Maybe they win if everyone is healthy. It’s a long season. This was the best the team has looked. We all know the platitudes.
  4. Luckily, though, I don’t have to do any of that, as New England outcoached and outplayed Buffalo to find themselves half a game out of first place in the AFC East. And this iteration of the Bills has never, at any point, defeated a defending AFC Champion.
  5. Let’s start with the offense, because that has been the team’s biggest weakness thus far. Sure, Maye had a fumble and a pick, but in a nice change of pace neither of them were on him. He probably should have felt the pressure on the strip sack and tucked the ball instead, but that was a strong pass rush against a new member of the offensive line. For the most part, Maye was decisive, poised, and clutch when he needed to be.
  6. I also have to point out that if T.J. Parker’s hands had been any more illegally to the face on that strip sack, he would have found himself on a split screen on MSNBC at some point this week being asked some questions.
  7. He also outrushed Josh Allen by 50 yards, which I didn’t expect (more on Allen’s legs and the defensive strategy surrounding that in a minute). And all of his runs were the right kind: receivers were covered, or the protection broke down, so he tucked and ran. He also got out of bounds or went right to the ground in the face of contact, which was even more enjoyable than watching him scramble.
  8. As for his leading receivers, it was a nice mix of old and new. Hunter Henry finally got involved in the passing game, and Romeo Doubs is getting more and more comfortable by the week. The bobble-to-interception wasn’t the best look for him, and he seems good for one drop per game. But if he can make up for it with two scores per game, I’ll certainly allow it.
  9. It’s wild to me how excited I was about the New England wide receiver room coming into this season. Brown, Doubs, Boutte, Douglas, Hollins, Chism, Williams… there just seemed to be so many weapons. Then Brown got hurt right away, Boutte got traded, Williams continues to be an absolute ghost, and a guy who should be thriving as WR4 was somehow pulling WR1 duty. And then that guy goes down too.
  10. “Man, if Mack Hollins can’t play for an extended period, this offense is really screwed” 100% went through my head yesterday. Football. What a ride!
  11. But in Hollins’s absence, seven different Patriots notched at least one reception. And Kyle Williams got two whole targets!
  12. I don’t want to get into too much turd in the punchbowlery in the wake of a big win. But what in the name of Tebow do the Patriots have to do to take a receiver early in the draft and have that receiver work out?
  13. And while I appreciate the universe balancing things out by consistently gifting the team with short, explosive, white slot receivers in the later rounds or through free agency, it would be nice if Kyle Williams could join the likes of Deion Branch and… um… Deion Branch… instead of Bethel Johnson, Chad Jackson, Brandon Tate, Taylor Price, Aaron Dobson, N’Keal Harry, Tyquan Thornton, and Ja’Lynn Polk.
  14. That said… I don’t want to pull the plug on Kyle Williams yet. He still has value and a skillset that could make him a strong contributor. But I also kind of feel like I’m at the point where, from this moment forward, if the Pats are thinking about targeting a WR in the draft, instead they should just trade that draft pick for a receiver who has already proven that he can produce at the NFL level.
  15. Speaking of producing… poor Tyquan Thornton. He had carved himself out a nice role in that Chiefs offense, which is a point in favor of the “it ain’t the player, it’s New England’s development” side of things. Hopefully that injury looks a lot worse than it is and he’ll be back on the field before too long.
  16. OK, enough with the negativity. One receiver being nonexistent just opened the door for the latest New England folk hero, Efton Chism III, who has made the catch of the year so far. This was shortly after high-pointing a crosser for a 19-yard gain to move the ball into Bills territory.
  17. There wasn’t anything complicated about the route; it looked like a simple out-and-up. Maye had to throw it a little earlier than he probably would have liked as the pressure came around the left side, and the coverage was perfect. Chism just made an absolutely absurd catch, and the legend was born.
  18. I was a little surprised to see that New England rushed for 143 yards yesterday. But then you realize that it’s less than 100 without Maye’s scrambles, and since TreVeyon Henderson seems to eat primarily off of long runs, it makes a lot more sense.
  19. Which means that this game was more or less won on the shoulders of the QB who had really been struggling through three weeks. And if he had laid another huge egg yesterday, there would be some conversations happening right now. Of that, I have no doubt. But this whole thing was just what everyone needed.
  20. There’s still a ton to clean up. This game could have gotten out of hand late in the first half with all the shenanigans that went down. But I’d rather need to clean up than start thinking about cleaning house.
  21. Speaking of cleaning house, the cupboard was pretty bare for the Patriots defense, who were without both Christians and a wildly depleted LB corp. They still held Allen to four yards rushing and should have recorded a safety.
  22. Seriously, what the hell was that? I guess a random, no-look throw to nobody while both still in the pocket in the end zone doesn’t meet the standards for grounding somehow.
  23. The best part about that play, though, was Gabe Jacas, who steamrolled Dion Dawkins and created immediate pressure. He’s still raw, but given the serious questions he was raising for everyone during the preseason, Jacas has been a beast.
  24. My only real gripe with the defense is that, at times, they seemed so concerned with Allen running that they broke into a lot of soft zone, which gave Allen plenty to choose from. But it was mostly effective, so hard to get too mad.
  25. I absolutely love it when the defense, any defense, celebrates an open receiver dropping a pass. As someone who has taken more than my fair share of credit for group projects in which I did zero work, it resonates with me on a personal level.
  26. I still remember being in 10th grade and, having done exactly nothing for our group report on FDR’s New Deal, offering to take everyone’s written notes and transcribe them onto a computer to make it presentable to the teacher. My dad had just purchased a voice-to-text program, and I spent all of 15 minutes reading everyone else’s notes as the computer did it’s thing. Work smart, not hard.
  27. Force an opening drive three-and-out and answer with an opening drive TD. Get an opening-drive TD on your first possession of the second half. Make big stops when necessary. Seal the game with a key interception and a ballsy rollout completion. Get a road win against a divisional opponent. Tough not to be happy today.

There’s still a lot of season left, and this has become a pattern with these two teams for some reason. Pats win in Buffalo early, then Buffalo wins at Gillette late. Hopefully this is the year we break that particular streak. But the Bills are out of our hair until December. Next on the dockett are the Raiders, Jets, Bears, and Dolphins. Those are all winnable games, and 5-3 or even 6-2 through October is very much possible. Just have to stay focused.

item.title: Cowboys at Texans Stock Report: CeeDee Lamb leads the way
item.description: Here is our Stock Report following Sunday’s Cowboys win
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys won the Texas State Championship on Sunday, and whether or not beating the in-state Houston Texans means anything extra to you, it stands to reason that wins in general do.

Sunday’s victory was very needed for the Cowboys to stop the bleeding that began down in Rio when they lost to the Baltimore Ravens. There is no rest for the weary though as they are back in action just a few days from now on Thursday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Before we fully shift focus to Tampa Bay, we need to properly tie a bow on the win in Houston. Several players really shined where others left us wanting more.

Here is our stock report from Sunday’s win. Let’s begin.

Stock Up: CeeDee Lamb

What can you really say at this point? CeeDee Lamb was a true and total alpha in Houston. He did whatever he wanted, and Next Gen Stats noted that he recorded multiple receptions against six different Texans defenders. Think about how absurd that is.

Lamb was entrusted with the game on the line, and well before it, to deliver and he absolutely did. He is living up to all hype and fanfare that people have had around him, and it feels like we are seeing the best version he has ever offered throughout his Cowboys career which is really saying something.

Stock Up: Joey Porter Jr.

It took all of five seconds for everyone involved to realize/remember that JPJ is the best cornerback on the Cowboys roster.

All told it was still a wading in for Porter as he was just acquired by the Cowboys this past week, but he played 19 snaps while in coverage and did not allow a single reception against a single target. It was evident that Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud was avoiding him at all costs.

That is what the Cowboys paid for. They went out to get someone to neutralize one side of the field, and they have it now.

Stock Up: Tyler Guyton

There really was a time, not too long ago, when we doubted whether or not Tyler Guyton would actually be the left tackle on this team. Heck, head coach Brian Schottenheimer openly declared in the offseason that Nate Thomas was competing with Guyton for the job. That is the same Nate Thomas who got traded to the Texans in roster cutdowns and was inactive for this game.

Having the left side of the offensive line so stable is such a peaceful thing. It will improve even more when Tyler Smith returns to the lineup. Don’t forget about that.

Stock Up: George Pickens

Four games into this season we have yet to see George Pickens have the exact same impact that CeeDee Lamb has, but he is easily making his mark.

Consider that the Cowboys’ game-winning drive would not have happened to the extent that it did without a huge gain from Pickens. Heck, consider that his 53-yard reception early in the second half was part of what woke the offense up at large. Pickens is giving the Cowboys his all and delivering when called upon.

Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy

This was arguably Ryan Flournoy’s best game since joining the Cowboys. The sample size there isn’t exactly large, but we have long believed that he could/should exist as a proper third option in the passing game and that’s exactly what he was in Houston.

Sometimes the opposing defense is taking so many things away and wreaking havoc in a number of different directions. You have to have that person who helps keep things moving right along, and that’s what Flo was in this game.

Stock Up: Quinnen Williams

The last two games have shown the Quinnen Williams who the Cowboys traded for and extended. He is turning into the defensive game-wrecker that his reputation said he was with the New York Jets.

Maybe it was a matter of gelling across time, but it feels fair to assume that this is the player who is here to stay. Clearly we hope that. is the case. Williams kept things in check, especially as the second half wore on and the game got tight. That’s his job and he did it very well.

Static Stock: Brian Schottenheimer

It has been a while since I handed out a static stock, but I believe Brian Schottenheimer is deserving in this instance.

The first half was pretty terrible. Specifically, the sequence at the end of it. Schottenheimer gambled in letting Brandon Aubrey attempt a 65-yard field goal right after having a 62-yard one blocked, and the miss gave Houston short field position that they converted into a field goal to send everyone to their respective locker rooms.

But Schotty locked in as the game wore on. He pledged all week to not let last week, as in the Ravens loss, define him. He said he would not hold the team back the way that he believed he did against Baltimore in Rio.

Eerily, the Cowboys faced almost an identical situation as the game wore on. Their offense went three and out when they could have iced the game with a four-point lead, and they took over with around two minutes left down by three. This time, unlike last, Schotty entrusted and enabled his superstars and the Cowboys won as a result. That is legitimate growth.

So the beginning was rough, but the end was great. So long as they are in that order and lead to a win, that’s what matters.

Stock Down: DaRon Bland

This is another instance where there really isn’t a ton to say. Joey Porter Jr. is incredible, but his incredible-ness means that opposing quarterbacks are going to attack DaRon Bland early and often. C.J. Stroud did so and was highly successful as a result of it.

There is no question that Bland is among the weaker points of the Cowboys roster at the moment. That is a huge issue that they are going to have to address if they don’t want to be in similar circumstances moving forward.

Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey

You can certainly argue that his 62-yard field goal was blocked because Will Anderson Jr. is incredible, and you can similarly claim that a 65-yard field goal is difficult to pull off and that being asked to do it right after a block is not ideal.

But it feels like we move the goalposts a lot for Aubrey, no pun intended. It feels like we let his reputation tell us we are being too harsh when moments of constructive criticism come up. It can be true that those circumstances were not ideal and that as the NFL’s highest-paid kicker he should be successful nonetheless. He wasn’t and that’s a problem.

Stock Down: Nick Sorensen

At the moment the Cowboys have one of the worst and least efficient special teams operations across the NFL. Nick Sorensen has been under fire even dating back to last year, and that temperature is only rising as a result of the messes we are seeing.

We regard the Cowboys’ special teams as great because of the visible pieces in the aforementioned Aubrey, KaVontae Turpin, and even Bryan Anger. But the operation is clunky. How? How can this really be possible?

Are they missing a veteran on the field in C.J. Goodwin? Does Nick Sorensen need to do more? Whatever the answer is, they have to find it immediately.

item.title: Lamar Jackson leaves in walking boot, to reportedly undergo MRI on ankle injury from Ravens win over Titans
item.description: Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game with an ankle injury and was replaced at the start of the second half by backup Tyler Huntley.
item.content:encoded:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and was replaced at the start of the second half by backup Tyler Huntley.

Per local reports, he left the stadium wearing a walking boot. He is reportedly set to undergo an MRI on the injury Monday, per ESPN.

Jackson was initially listed as questionable to return with the injury, but he remained sidelined for the rest of the game. The Ravens went scoreless without him after halftime and fended off a Titans rally from a 24-7 halftime deficit.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that the team doesn't "know enough about" Jackson's injury to provide a precise diagnosis, but said that the Ravens considered bringing him back into the game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported after the game that Jackson is considered day-to-day with the injury.

Jackson ankle rolled on sack

Jackson appeared to sustain the injury on a sack late in the first half. Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson chased Jackson down from behind for a sack on the final offensive play of the first half. Jackson was able to stand up from the tackle and walk off the field. It wasn't apparent in the moment that he'd sustained an injury.

Jermaine with the sack

📺: @NFLonCBSpic.twitter.com/zL6SHLHckO

— Tennessee Titans (@Titans) October 4, 2026

But slow-motion replay showed that Jackson's left ankle got caught up and twisted under Johnson's body as Johnson sacked him from behind. And Jackson didn't return to the game.

Lamar Jackson is now questionable to return with an ankle injury pic.twitter.com/76w3ptv6PO

— NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026

Baltimore led 24-7 when Huntley took over at quarterback, reducing pressure on Baltimore's offense before a stagnant second half forced the Ravens to consider putting Jackson back in the game.

Jackson off to another MVP-like start to the season

With the win, Baltimore joined the Cleveland Browns at 3-1 atop the AFC North. Jackson, of course, is a significant piece of Baltimore's hopes in the division and beyond. He was off to another strong start to his season prior to Sunday's injury.

Jackson entered Sunday's game having completed 69.7% of his passes for 248.3 yards per game with 4 touchdowns and 1 interception. He led the NFL in both yards per attempt (9.8) and yards per completion (14.1). He'd added 124 yards (7.3 ypa) and 1 touchdown on the ground.

Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns in the first half against the Titans.

The Ravens are certainly hoping that Jackson's injury won't linger. Baltimore has upcoming games against the Falcons, Browns, Bengals, Bills and Jaguars.

item.title: The Colts won, but Daniel Jones needs to get a grip
item.description: The Colts should be wary of Jones’ recent turnovers.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts found some much-needed fortune in London as they managed to beat the Washington Commanders and climb to 2-2. Yes, there was skill and preparation involved, but there was a lot of luck as well. Daniel Jones tested that luck throughout the game, but if the Colts are going to keep winning, they need to reserve some in the tank. The best way to do that is for Jones to stop turning the ball over. 

Jones fumbled on the second play of the game in a highly unusual fashion. It wasn’t as bizarre as the “butt fumble”, but it looked just as sloppy. The defender bull rushed Bernhard Raimann and had them both in Jones’ face, but to fumble the ball like that was simply odd. Just like against the Texans, he threw off his back foot under pressure and was intercepted. It was a dispiriting quarter and a half as the offense was dreadful.

Luckily, the Colts weathered the early storm. The defense held strong and kept the Commanders out of the endzone to limit the damage to six. Additionally, facing a third string quarterback didn’t hurt either. That isn’t always going to be the case, however. The better teams in this league will make the Colts pay for their errors. Jones has to be better. He has to protect the ball and play smarter. He cannot turn the ball over at this rate if the Colts hope to survive.

Daniel Jones has seven turnovers across four games with five in the last two. That looks like the second half of 2025 Jones, but the Colts can’t win with that version. An occasional turnover is understandable, but at least two of the fumbles and both of the interceptions were avoidable. Those must be cleaned up. Jones has to find a way to get a grip.
